learn.canDo: Explain a branch as a pointer into a graph of immutable commits, and keep work reachable so it survives gc.
learn.why: 'I lost my commits' is one of the most common Git panics. Knowing reachability removes most of the fear.
learn.keyIdea: A branch is a label on a commit.

learn.canDo: Compare merge, rebase and squash by history shape, conflicts and bisect granularity, and never rewrite shared history.
learn.why: Teams argue about this constantly. The judgement is knowing what each rewrites and who it affects.
learn.keyIdea: Never rewrite what others are standing on.

learn.canDo: Choose between soft, mixed and hard reset by what each keeps, and cherry-pick a fix to another branch.
learn.why: A forum command that deletes uncommitted work is a rite of passage. Knowing the three areas avoids it.
learn.keyIdea: Move the label. Keep the work.

learn.canDo: Recover lost commits with the reflog, fsck and a remote copy, and know what Git never recorded.
learn.why: The calm way to answer 'I deleted it' is knowing the windows. Pushing early beats all of them.
learn.keyIdea: Find the hash, then give it a name.

chapter.story: A teammate deletes a branch, a rebase goes wrong, and the team learns what Git actually stores.
outcomes: Choose between merge, rebase and squash
Pick the right reset and move a single fix
chapter.why: Git is a database of snapshots with names on top. Once you see the shape, almost every mistake is recoverable and every workflow debate has a clear trade-off.
chapter.payoff: In an interview you can explain Git's model and its rules of thumb. At work you will fix a bad rebase calmly.
